summary: ethers-lib postinstall exfiltrates installer secrets and wallet material to a hardcoded Pipedream endpoint
details: ethers-lib@1.0.1 is a typosquat of the `ethers` package whose `index.js` merely re-exports the real `ethers` module. Its `postinstall` script runs automatically on `npm install` and reads classic installer-side secret files — `.env*`, `.npmrc`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`/`id_ed25519`/`id_ecdsa`, Solana keypairs, Ethereum keystores under `~/.ethereum/keystore`, and `.gitconfig` — plus a recursive scan of dotfile directories under `$HOME` matching the regex `/wallet|key|secret|seed|mnemonic|keystore|private/i`. The collected file contents are serialized as JSON and POSTed over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint `https://enxhcjpo5ev.x.pipedream.net`. The re-export of `ethers` acts as a cover story so the package appears functional to a developer who installed it by mistake.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
